current_answer: As of 19 September 2026 at 12:00 UTC, no broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven. OpenAI, Claude, and xAI status pages are calm, but fresh public evidence is concentrated in the system around the models: one Codex Desktop task processed 242.3 million tokens and moved the weekly allowance by 11 percentage points without a task-wide warning; new access and entitlement reports blocked work before model quality could be judged; and a Gemini external-URL file-input path recovered after a provider response. These are real user-facing changes, not broad weight evidence. Record a fixed task symptom, baseline, route or entitlement receipt, context, outcome, and reversible action before switching or calling degradation.

catalogue_card.question: Are popular AI models getting worse right now?
catalogue_card.text: No broad model decline is proven. A large Codex task-budget failure and fresh access or entitlement leads make the system around the model the urgent watch lane.

summary: No broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven; current provider status is calm but status is not task quality.
A Codex Desktop report says one task processed 242.3 million tokens and moved weekly usage by 11 points without a task-wide warning, projected-cost notice, or automatic stop.
Fresh Codex reports show managed Work Cloud authentication failure, prolonged non-response, and Windows context or session trouble before quality could be tested.
A Gemini external-URL file-input path appears to have recovered after provider discussion; this is a narrow backend or permission lane, not model evidence.
Claude complaints and counterreports plus Google entitlement friction show demand for a structured task, plan, platform, time, and receipt intake.
Langfuse and Braintrust show private observability pressure around traces, evals, scoring, cost, thresholds, alerts, and regression datasets.
Reader move: define the symptom, baseline, budget, threshold, receipt, and reversible action, then record requested and served model, route, context, outcome, and allowance.
uncertainty: No matched longitudinal task series, provider-served-model receipt, provider ledger, representative denominator, recovered-time measure, human pilot, or willingness-to-pay evidence is available.
Status pages constrain declared availability; issue and forum reports identify narrow access or backend paths; community reports remain self-selected.
The 242.3 million-token event is a detailed allowance and orchestration report, not a core capability test.
The alert contract is still untested with an independent live baseline or a real operator decision.
freshness_note: Fresh public-source research completed 19 September 2026. The broad call remains no capability decline proven, while task-budget safeguards, managed access, entitlement, and recovered backend paths are now explicit evidence lanes.
